summary: Canefield Airport (DCF) is a small regional airport situated near the western coast of Dominica, just a few kilometers north of the capital city Roseau. It serves as the island's secondary airport, primarily handling small regional aircraft and inter-island flights within the Caribbean. The airport sits in a lush tropical valley, offering passengers immediate access to the Roseau area and the surrounding attractions of this nature-rich island.
faqs:
Q: What is the main airline that operates at Canefield Airport?
A: Canefield Airport has historically been served by small regional carriers, including interCaribbean Airways and LIAT, offering connections to nearby Caribbean islands such as Martinique and Guadeloupe.

Q: How far is Canefield Airport from Roseau?
A: The airport is located approximately 5 kilometers north of Roseau, making it a short drive of about 10-15 minutes to the capital city center.

Q: Are there car rental services available at Canefield Airport?
A: Limited car rental services and taxis are available at the airport, though it is advisable to arrange transportation in advance, especially for travelers heading to more remote areas of the island.

Q: Can large aircraft land at Canefield Airport?
A: No, Canefield has a short runway suitable only for small propeller aircraft and regional jets, which is why larger international flights use Douglas-Charles Airport on the other side of the island.
transport_tips: Taxis and private shuttles are the most reliable way to reach the airport, with the short drive to Roseau typically costing a modest fare. Renting a car is a good option if you plan to explore Dominica's interior, as the island's road network connects well from the airport area. Arrange your return transfer in advance, as taxi availability can be limited during off-peak hours.
local_tip: If you have a wait at Canefield, walk or take a short taxi ride to the nearby Canefield area to enjoy a local snack at one of the small rum shops. Frequented by locals, these spots offer an authentic taste of Dominican culture, including fresh juices and a chance to chat with residents who can share insider tips on the best hiking trails and hidden beaches.
